title: Launch planning for Hosted overload protection (comms, changelog, support enablement)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
body:
## Summary
We are rolling out overload protection (edge admission control + routing circuit breakers + runtime shedding) for Hosted API. This ticket tracks launch planning: customer-facing comms, changelog language, support enablement, and internal readiness gates.

The intent is to improve behavior during overload (fewer ambiguous 5xx/timeouts; more consistent 429/503 with Retry-After + Redwood error codes) while preventing cascade failures. We need to set expectations, document retry guidance, and ensure Support/CS have clear playbooks.

## Goals
- Customers understand what changed and how to respond (Retry-After semantics, recommended backoff + jitter, what errors mean).
- Support is ready with macros, troubleshooting steps, and a consistent explanation of billing impact.
- Changelog + docs updates land before broad rollout.
- Status-page language is aligned (don’t call load shedding an outage, but do communicate elevated overload-shedding events when customer impact is material).

## Non-goals
- Not redefining quotas / rate limits (this complements them).
- Not publishing internal thresholds/capacity specifics.

## Target audiences
1) Self-serve Hosted developers (SDK + OpenAI-compat)
2) Enterprise Hosted customers (high traffic/spiky)
3) Dedicated customers (avoid confusion: Dedicated behavior differs; align wording)
4) Support + CS + on-call

## Key messages (draft)
- During traffic spikes or regional capacity constraints, Redwood may return:
  - HTTP 429 (overload admission control / fair-share shedding)
  - HTTP 503 (temporary capacity protection / breaker open)
  - Response includes a Redwood error code + Retry-After header when applicable
- These are protective responses; they are preferable to timeouts/ambiguous 5xx.
- Recommended client behavior: exponential backoff with jitter; honor Retry-After; avoid immediate retries / tight loops.
- If configured/available, the platform may safely degrade via fallback policies (model/region/tier) without changing the API surface.

## Deliverables
### A) Customer comms plan
- Changelog entry (public)
- Docs updates (public + internal)
- Targeted email for enterprise accounts that historically hit overload (optional; coordinate w/ CS)
- Status-page “overload shedding active” template + guidance for when to post

### B) Support enablement
- Support macro(s) for 429/503 overload errors:
  - What it means
  - How to parse Redwood error code
  - Retry guidance examples
  - When to escalate to SRE (what to collect: request IDs, region, model, timestamps)
- Internal FAQ: billing/usage implications (confirm: shed requests should not be billed; if any exceptions exist, document explicitly)
- Training session (30 min) w/ Support + CS: walk through new error taxonomy + common client mistakes (retry loops, no jitter, parallel retries)

### C) Launch readiness checklist (go/no-go)
- SDKs surface Retry-After + Redwood codes cleanly (Python/TS/Go)
- Docs published: error taxonomy page + retry guide
- Support macros published + pinned
- Status-page rules aligned with SRE on what constitutes an incident vs protective shedding
- Canary results reviewed: customer ticket volume, 429/503 distribution, p99 latency improvement

## Timeline proposal (align to ENG-4834 rollout)
- Week 0 (pre-canary): finalize wording + docs PRs + support macros
- Canary start (us-east; 1–2 models):
  - Day 1: internal announcement + what to watch
  - Day 3: review metrics + top customer impacts
  - Day 5: decide expand / tune
- Pre-global rollout: publish changelog + optional proactive note to top 10 traffic accounts
- Post-global rollout: 2-week monitoring window + support ticket review; feed into ENG-4841

## Draft changelog copy (v0)
"Improved resilience during traffic spikes: Hosted API now returns more consistent overload responses (e.g., 429/503 with Retry-After) to protect latency and prevent timeouts. See docs for recommended retry/backoff guidance."

Open question: do we mention "circuit breakers" explicitly, or keep it customer-oriented (recommended).

## Open questions / decisions needed
1) Comms threshold: When do we post to status page? (e.g., sustained shed rate > X% for Y mins, multi-region, or high enterprise impact)
2) Billing: confirm definitively whether overload-protected responses are excluded from billed usage and how it appears in console usage analytics.
3) Dedicated alignment: confirm if Dedicated will ever emit identical 429/503 overload codes vs separate semantics; ensure docs highlight differences without implying Dedicated is "worse".
4) OpenAI-compat: confirm wording doesn’t confuse customers expecting OpenAI-style error objects; link to compatibility doc.

## Owners / collaborators
- PM owner: Henry Cho
- Product lead (Hosted): Nikhil Sharma
- SRE input: Rafael Mendes / Sean Gallagher
- Support readiness: Dev Patel (+ Owen Phillips)
- Status page & transparency: Nora Ahmed
- Docs: Elliot Price / Wei Chen
- Dedicated alignment: Lauren Bishop

## Links (working set)
- PRD/requirements: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-hosted-overload-protection-customer-experience.json
- Support doc draft: sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-client-retry-guidance.json
- Status template: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/template-overload-event-communication.json
- Initiative umbrella: sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821.json

## Acceptance criteria
- Changelog text approved by Hosted PM + SRE lead + Support lead
- Support macros published and reviewed; training completed; recording/link posted
- Docs published before global rollout
- Status-page criteria documented and agreed with on-call; linked from runbook
comments: 2025-12-03 (Henry Cho): Drafted initial comms outline + changelog v0. Syncing with Dev Patel on support macro format and with Nora Ahmed on status criteria.

2025-12-06 (Dev Patel): Support request: please include 2 concrete retry examples (simple exponential backoff w/ jitter; honoring Retry-After) and a short section on common client anti-patterns (parallel retries, zero jitter).

2025-12-09 (Rafael Mendes): Strong preference to avoid the word "outage" when shedding is functioning as designed. Suggest phrasing: "We are actively shedding excess traffic to protect platform latency" and provide Retry-After guidance. We should only status-post when customer impact is sustained and significant.
2025-12-12 (Wei Chen): Docs plan: add a dedicated "Overload errors" page and cross-link from rate limits + reliability section. Need final error-code list from ADR-0147 so wording stays stable.

2025-12-18 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated alignment note: Dedicated pools may still shed under extreme saturation, but expectations differ (contracted capacity). Ensure docs clearly separate Hosted default behavior vs Dedicated, and advise Dedicated customers to contact support if seeing sustained overload errors.

2026-01-07 (Henry Cho): Updated changelog language to emphasize customer benefit (fewer timeouts, clearer retries). Added draft status-page criteria for review: post if shed rate > 5% for 15+ min affecting >1 region OR if a named enterprise account is blocked for >10 min.

2026-01-12 (Nikhil Sharma): Please route final comms through Support + SRE sign-off before publishing. Also confirm billing behavior: overload-protected responses should not be billed; if there’s any edge case, document explicitly.
